title: A zone claim is only as strong as every crossing
question: Which crossing actually enforces research-to-production access, and which alternate route breaks the isolation claim?
scenario: A research workstation needs one analytics operation against production. The approved route crosses a policy enforcement point into a broker, which uses a scoped service identity. Administrators use a separate logged management zone. A backup appliance on that management subnet can also reach production directly through a stale broad exception.
focalRelation: Zone names describe purpose. Each crossing must name source, destination, direction, action, policy identity, enforcement point, evidence, and failure behavior; a privileged or alternate route can invalidate an otherwise correct segmentation claim.

nodes.label: Research workstation
nodes.detail: Untrusted research-zone host requesting one documented analytics operation.

nodes.label: Research crossing PEP
nodes.detail: Evaluates source identity, destination, protocol, and approved analytics action; direct production access stops here.

nodes.label: Analytics broker
nodes.detail: Exposes only the approved operation and uses a scoped service identity toward production.

nodes.label: Production dataset
nodes.detail: The production dataset accepts the broker’s scoped service identity and the separately authorized administrator path; it denies direct research access, while the stale backup exception remains an evidenced bypass.

nodes.label: Brokered administrator path
nodes.detail: A named administrator receives authenticated, time-limited access through a broker that enforces and records approved administration; management-zone location alone grants no privilege.

nodes.label: Backup appliance
nodes.detail: Shares the management subnet but has a stale rule permitting direct production reachability outside the broker; its path lacks the broker’s flow and policy evidence.

nodes.label: Evidence comparison
nodes.detail: Places the research PEP’s local crossing record beside the management broker’s local administrator-session record without treating either policy point as the source or destination of the other record.

lanes.label: Research zone
lanes.rule: Zone membership supplies context but never grants production access.

lanes.label: Research-to-production crossing
lanes.rule: Only the explicitly permitted direction, protocol, identity, and action pass.

lanes.label: Production zone
lanes.rule: Production accepts the broker’s scoped request, not arbitrary research traffic.

lanes.label: Management zone
lanes.rule: Every privileged identity and route remains separately authorized and observed; unbrokered paths are gaps.

states.title: Purpose before proof
states.caption: Research, production, and management zones state intended trust purposes. No enclosure or subnet label proves enforcement.

statuses.research: The research workstation remains an untrusted workload in the research zone.
statuses.production: The production dataset remains a protected resource in the production zone.
statuses.management: The administrator path is privileged and requires policy and evidence distinct from the research flow.

states.title: The brokered action crosses explicitly
states.caption: The research request reaches the enforcement point, which permits only the named operation to the broker; the broker uses a scoped identity at production.

statuses.enforcement: The enforcement point permits only the named analytics action and denies direct research-to-production access.
statuses.broker: The analytics broker uses a service identity scoped to the approved production operation.
statuses.research: Untrusted research-zone host requesting one documented analytics operation.
statuses.production: The production dataset accepts the broker’s scoped service identity and the separately authorized administrator path; it denies direct research access, while the stale backup exception remains an evidenced bypass.

states.title: Enforcement leaves evidence
states.caption: Permit, deny, and privileged decisions are recorded by the policy points. VLAN, VRF, VPN, or zero-trust labels remain design mechanisms whose operation must be observed.

statuses.enforcement: The enforcement point records both the approved research request and denied direct attempts.
statuses.management: The management broker records the authenticated, time-limited administrator session.
statuses.evidence-accounting: The comparison keeps the two local records distinct while checking that each crossing produced the evidence its own policy requires.

states.title: The alternate route breaks the claim
states.caption: The backup appliance reaches production without the privileged broker. Its trusted subnet label does not authorize the flow; the stale exception must be removed or replaced by explicitly equivalent enforcement.

statuses.backup: The backup appliance uses an unauthorized alternate crossing with no broker decision evidence.
statuses.management: The stale backup rule bypasses the brokered administrator path.
statuses.production: The production dataset accepts the broker’s scoped service identity and the separately authorized administrator path; it denies direct research access, while the stale backup exception remains an evidenced bypass.

variants.label: Management-subnet bypass
variants.changedFact: The backup appliance sits in the named management subnet but bypasses the broker through a stale broad rule.

lanes.label: Management subnet
lanes.rule: Subnet membership supplies route context and never grants administrative authority.

lanes.label: Production crossing
lanes.rule: Every source, destination, action, protocol, and duration requires an explicit enforcement decision.

lanes.label: Production zone
lanes.rule: Only brokered or equivalently constrained and logged operations may reach production.

nodes.label: Backup appliance
nodes.detail: The appliance shares the management subnet but has no blanket authority over production.

nodes.label: Management-subnet membership
nodes.detail: The network location provides routing context, not authorization for every production action.

nodes.label: Stale broad firewall rule
nodes.detail: An old exception permits direct backup-appliance reachability to production outside the broker.

nodes.label: Broker or equivalent PEP
nodes.detail: A named enforcement point restricts appliance identity, destination, protocol, action, and duration.

nodes.label: Production dataset
nodes.detail: The dataset must accept only the authorized backup operation through an evidenced control.

nodes.label: Crossing decision evidence
nodes.detail: Logs prove which appliance action was permitted, denied, expired, and reviewed.

states.title: The subnet label hides a crossing
states.caption: The appliance is in the management subnet, but a stale broad rule gives it a direct production path outside the broker.

statuses.backup: The backup appliance has a direct route that exceeds its documented operation.
statuses.subnet: Management-subnet membership supplies location, not authority.
statuses.stale-rule: The stale broad rule creates an actual unbrokered path.
statuses.production: Production is reachable without a scoped broker decision.

states.title: Replace the broad route with enforcement
states.caption: Remove the stale exception and route the named backup operation through the broker or an equivalent policy enforcement point.

statuses.backup: The appliance requests only the approved backup operation.
statuses.broker: The enforcement point checks appliance identity, destination, action, protocol, and duration.
statuses.production: Production accepts only the scoped and authorized operation.

states.title: Verify the crossing
states.caption: Crossing evidence must show permits, denials, expiry, and review; changing the subnet name would prove none of these.

statuses.broker: The enforcement point records each production crossing decision.
statuses.production: The dataset is no longer reachable through the stale broad rule.
statuses.evidence: The record supports testing of source, destination, action, duration, and outcome.

prediction.prompt: A route test confirms that the backup appliance can reach production without the privileged broker. What conclusion follows?

options.label: The isolation claim is incomplete until the alternate route is removed or equivalently enforced and logged
options.feedback: Correct. The direct route is an alternate crossing that bypasses the claimed enforcement and logging path.

options.label: The broker’s scoped identity proves the approved route covers every production crossing
options.feedback: The scoped identity supports one route. It does not govern the backup appliance’s separate direct path.

options.label: Management-subnet membership makes the direct route an authorized crossing
options.feedback: A subnet label supplies location context, not authority. The direct route still needs an explicit identity, action, enforcement, and evidence decision.

prediction.hint: A zone label supplies context; enforcement decides whether a crossing is authorized.

transfer.prompt: The backup appliance sits in the named management subnet but bypasses the broker. What should the architect do?

options.label: Rename the subnet trusted-backup so the exception matches its intended purpose
options.feedback: Renaming changes documentation, not reachability, authorization, enforcement, or evidence.

options.label: Keep the route because management-subnet membership proves administrative authority
options.feedback: A subnet label is not authorization. The appliance identity, destinations, actions, and evidence still require an enforcement decision.

options.label: Model the route as a crossing, restrict it, and enforce the broker or an equivalent logged control
options.feedback: Correct. The bypass becomes explicit, gets bounded policy, and can be tested against the original isolation claim.

transfer.hint: The backup appliance’s stale rule is an actual path that bypasses the broker.

retry.prompt: The routine route is removed and the teams call the environments air-gapped, but approved removable media still carries updates into production. Which conclusion is accurate?

options.label: Call the zone air-gapped and leave update media unapproved, uninspected, bidirectional, and unrecorded.
options.feedback: The permitted media movement is still a crossing. Separation does not govern the media, update provenance, scanning, or evidence.

options.label: Treat the media path as a governed crossing with authorization, inspection, direction, and evidence
options.feedback: Correct. The boundary remains useful only when every permitted transfer mechanism has explicit controls and failure behavior.

options.label: Treat removable media as equivalent to a VPN without governing custody, contents, direction, destination, or evidence.
options.feedback: A VPN is a tunnel with defined endpoints and selectors. Removable media has different custody, provenance, scanning, and transfer controls.

retry.hint: Remove or constrain the bypass and record source, destination, action, duration, and outcome.

takeaway: A zone is a declared purpose, not proof. Validate every normal, denied, privileged, and alternate crossing at its actual enforcement point and through its evidence.
assumptions: Arrow direction is request direction; a blocked edge stops before the protected resource.
The stale backup exception is a hypothetical configuration fact, not a claim about a specific product.
VLAN, VPN, VRF, micro-segmentation, air gaps, and zero-trust policy create different boundaries and dependencies.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The boundary states preserve permitted, denied, brokered-management, evidenced, bypass, and removable-media crossings. Learners step among authored crossing cases rather than selecting arbitrary crossing modes.
